Lucy Letby - Cross-examination Day 7: Babies K, F & L Juror sent home unwell
CONTENTS
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Housekeeping
Monday, 5 June 2023
(Delay in proceedings)
(In the absence of the jury)
I'm sorry about the slight delay. On Wednesday, I'll say this now and I'll say it to the jury when they come in, we'll finish no later than 3 pm: a juror has a medical appointment. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Good morning. Sorry about the slight delay.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: On Wednesday we will be finishing no later than 3 o'clock in the afternoon. All right? I'm aware of the other issue which affects one of you and we'll wait and see what happens in relation to that. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just having had the opportunity over the weekend to think about what it is you've said on Friday, and indeed before that, is there anything that you would like to review?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we go to tile 104, please, in the [Baby K] sequence. This is something that we touched on briefly on Friday. This was your admission record for [Baby K]; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The record shows that it was opened at 06.04 and ended at 06.10. We can see that second time there at the top of the page.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I asked you about the care of the endotracheal tube, which of course was highly relevant to [Baby K], wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you insert that data, "Patient has an artificial airway"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, so part of the -- to obtain that care plan you have to tick certain boxes of equipment that the baby has attached to them, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And as a result of you ticking that box, what did the machine then produce in terms of information?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The parts underneath.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. And what are they, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Secure ETT to taped bonnet. Retie tapes with two nurses in case of accidental extubation. Record tube size and length. Monitor patient's tolerance of ET tube to aid compliance."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And we know that within 5 minutes of you entering that data, [Baby K]'s tube displaced again, don't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. And that you were with [Baby K] between you closing that entry and her desaturating again?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't say that, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why can't you say that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Because I've no memory of being at [Baby K]'s cot side.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Well, what would you normally do with the records once you'd booked her in?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Take them back to the nursery or give them to the member of staff looking after the baby.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You'd put them back at the cot side, wouldn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Or give them to a member of staff, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This was [Baby K]'s second desaturation. We'll come to the first at the end. Do you remember me explaining that to you on Friday?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You will remember, I'm sure, that a morphine infusion had been running since 03.50 that morning.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And so by the time [Baby K] desaturated on this second occasion, she was well sedated; would you agree?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The morphine had been running for 5 minutes short of 2.5 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And yet the tube slipped again at 06.15?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, just after you'd been with her. Do you agree with that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't say that I was physically with [Baby K], no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I don't have any recollection of being with [Baby K], no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where had you got the notes from?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's different to being in -- physically touching [Baby K]. The notes are kept on a trolley at the end of the bedside, they're not physically with the baby. So I can't say that I was physically with [Baby K], touching [Baby K].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Presumably, if you took the notes back, and there was some issue on the monitor you would have seen it, wouldn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If there was, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. I'd like to move on to [Baby K]'s third desaturation before we come to the one involving Dr Jayaram when he says you saw you standing over her; okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This was a desaturation at about 07.30 that morning, 07.25. Do you remember it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember saying to the jury in answer to your own counsel that you had nothing to do with this desaturation?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I don't have any recollection of at all, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, is that the same as having nothing to do with it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall any intervention at that point, no, so I can't say.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember the evidence of [Nurse B] on 1 March about this?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember the reason that she said her attention was drawn to this third desaturation of [Baby K]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, she said I called to her from the nursery.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. What were you doing in nursery 1 at 07.30?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't answer that. I don't have any recollection of that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What should you have been doing at 07.30 that morning?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We would be preparing for handover.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where were the babies that you were handing over?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Nursery 2, is it?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So the question is: what were you doing in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, I can't answer that. Staff go between the nurseries all the time.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, but why would you be -- I'm interested: it's all very well saying staff go between the nurseries all the time, but what were you doing in the nursery at that time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't answer that because I don't have a specific memory, so I can't answer that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, let's look at the neonatal review, please, which I think is still open in front of you. Can we look at page 7 of 9, please, to look at what you were doing in the half hour before [Baby K] desaturated for the third time.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: In the bottom third or so of the page, can you see there's quite a lot of blue font?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If you go to line 232, do you see that half an hour or 25 minutes or so before [Baby K] desaturated, you were attending to AR?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And AR was one of your children in nursery 2?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just remind ourselves at page 2 of 9 of who your other child or other designated child was. It was GT; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And we see that the last mention of GT before [Baby K]'s desaturation, which is shown at line 238, your last recorded contact with GT was at line 227 at 06.49 --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- where you were co-signing for medication that was given to her at that point?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So there was no reason, was there, for you to have been in nursery 1 at 07.30?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't answer that now because, as I've said, there's many reasons why staff would enter another nursery.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, let's concentrate on the two children that you were designated to look after, please, GT and AR.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You've had access to their medical records, haven't you, as part of this process?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is there anything in their medical records that suggests there was something going on at 7.30 which would have necessitated you being in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You've told us, and we've heard from many witnesses, that the handover begins at about 7.30.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And so the question is, why were you in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't answer that question.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The answer, Lucy Letby, is that you were sabotaging [Baby K] yet again, weren't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why didn't you make a note of what happened at 07.30?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't recall that happening.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Sorry?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't recall this event happening.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: No, but do you accept it happened?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I have no memory, so I cannot say either way.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember your colleague [Nurse B] giving evidence about it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And it was not disputed with her, was it, that this event had happened and that you had called her to nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, but I can't categorically say whether that did or didn't happen. I have no memory.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But she categorically says it did, didn't she, and you didn't dispute it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you dispute it in your defence statement?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I say I have no memory.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were you trying to create the impression that [Baby K] habitually moved her own tube?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Was [Baby K] a baby who more than once moved her own tube?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't answer that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why can't you answer it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Because I can't say how the tubes have dislodged if that's what's happened.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, did you have a memory of [Baby K]'s tube moving more than once?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: From reading the notes, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. I don't quite understand the answer, that answer. What do you mean?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't have an independent memory of the tube slipping, no. It's only through police interviews, being informed that it slipped several times and looking at the notes that I recalled that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'm going to give you in a moment a rather fuller version of your interview, but if you could just get the interview bundle number 2, please, and go to the second of the [Baby K] interviews, so this is the interview of 12 June 2019. The extract that begins at [Initials of Baby K] 6. The time on 12 June was 09.51.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just take as much time as you need to orientate yourself, but do you see at page 6 at the beginning of this interview, the police were asking you about Joanne Williams leaving the unit to update [Baby K]'s parents?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We know that that was at 3.47 from the door swipe data, don't we? Do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then on the next page, the police were asking about Dr Jayaram, which is something that I'm going to come to in a moment.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Got that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then at the bottom of the page the officer says to you:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Dr Jayaram states that [Baby K]'s ET tube had become dislodged and there was no fault with the ventilator and the tube was replaced. He goes on to clarify that a tube can become dislodged if a baby is active and moving around."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do you see that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then over the page, please, on to page 8. They then start to ask you another question but you talk across them and say:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I didn't dislodge her tube."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You then say:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I believe earlier in the shift her tube had slipped and she's already had her tube replaced earlier in the shift."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What were you talking about there?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So there I was talking about a previous -- I'd got the dates wrong. I'm referring to an incident with Mel Taylor on a previous shift where the tube had slipped, because that was the notes that I had at that time.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We're talking about [Baby K].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: [Baby K] was only in the Countess of Chester from about some time after 2 o'clock on the 17th.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. I think in one of my interviews, though, I was given the evidence of Mel Taylor; is that not right?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'm asking you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, I can't -- without reading through this now, I can't see... I'm not sure.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were you there trying to create the impression with the police that [Baby K] was a child who habitually displaced her own tube?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. But she had -- it had come out more than once, I believe, from the notes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Oh, it did, because on three occasions, we suggest, you deliberately displaced it --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I did not.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- because you were trying to kill her.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you dispute the evidence of [Nurse B] regarding that desaturation at 7.30 or thereabouts?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Again, I don't think I can comment on whether that's the truth or not. I just have no memory of it. That's not for me to say whether she's accurate or not. I have no recollection.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You're lying about that, aren't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If you were there, as described by [Nurse B], would you normally have made a note?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If I... If I was there, no, I can't -- no, not necessarily, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why did you make a note in the case of [Baby I] on 13 October then?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: In relation to what?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The desaturation in the dark with Ashleigh Hudson.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Because that was a life-threatening event that I'd come across.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So was this.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I then took over [Baby I]'s care.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So this is for a child of 25 weeks, isn't it, 25 weeks' gestation, wouldn't you say?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't answer that. I can't remember it.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It was left for Mel Taylor to make a note, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't recall.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, I'll remind you. It's tile 166. If we go on to the document, please. Turn it sideways. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I've got the wrong reference here. Let me just check.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Pause)
While we check the reference, can I just assist with one matter as a matter of record, my Lord?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We're jumping around between the counts. On 13 October with [Baby I], just going to the notes quickly, care was actually transferred by Ashleigh Hudson or from Ashleigh Hudson to Ms Letby, hence Ms Letby made a note. She was just asked why she didn't make notes with [Baby K], but as I follow it care wasn't transferred in the same way. It might be a bit much to expect her to recall back to what the notes say on 13 October, so I'm just pointing that out now as to the reason for the note on the 13th with [Baby I].
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Anyway, let's go to the desaturation at 03.50.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'd like to start by going back to the neonatal review, please, which is underneath your interview bundle there.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So if we go to page 5 of 9, please. If we look at lines 115 and 116, do we see there that you were conducting observations of and feeding the child GT?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And GT was in nursery 2?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This was a feed of 55ml of milk?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Which I think you've told us would take about 20 minutes or thereabouts?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Approximately, yes. I think she was offered a bottle at that feed as well.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Do you have a memory of this?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. Not a direct memory, no, just reading from the charts.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. I just want to see what you agree with and what you disagree with; okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you agree that Joanne Williams was [Baby K]'s designated nurse on this shift?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you agree that she, that is Joanne Williams, left [Baby K] at 03.47?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I agree that she left her. I don't think I can say the specific minute that Jo left.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, from memory perhaps not, but from the evidence -- I think it's tile 63, if we can go to that, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is the swipe data. Do you remember you being referred to this --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- by your own counsel?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I just couldn't recall the exact digits.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It's all right, I'm not criticising you for not being able to remember a precise tile number or time even.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: But you may remember this is the one where, when you were being asked questions about your own counsel, there was a mistake made about which way Joanne Williams was going.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It was suggested to you that she was coming into the neonatal unit, whereas this shows she was leaving the unit.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And so do you accept that she left the unit at that time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you accept that at that time Dr Jayaram was sitting at the nurses' station?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Again, I can't answer that because I don't have any recollection. I can't recall Dr Jayaram's whereabouts.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Okay. Well, let's look at the evidence. Tile 59, please. These are notes made by somebody in a different hospital; okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: As always, if you want to go to the originals, which are behind this, we can go to them. We've shown them already in the course of the evidence, but this was somebody from the transport team who was speaking to Dr Jayaram on the phone.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is there a phone at the nurses' station?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: There is, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And this is timed by that person 6 minutes before Joanne Williams left to go to speak to [Mother of Baby K].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And so with that in mind, do you accept that Dr Jayaram was at the nurses' station?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Again, I don't know how I can answer that because I can't -- that's reliant on his account. I have no recollection to say whether that did or didn't happen.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But if that is correct and he was sat at the nurses' station on at that specific phone then, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just so we understand, how many phones are there that somebody from an external source could ring into the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: There's four phones on the unit.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where are they?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: There's one in nursery 1 and then there's three outside on the nursing station.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. So if the -- where do external calls usually come in, the nursing station or nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Usually the portable phone at the nursing station, but it's a portable phone so I can't 100% say that it was answered at the desk.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: No, but we know what he says about it anyway, don't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you dispute that, given [Baby K]'s condition, her age, her extreme prematurity, that Joanne Williams would have asked one of her colleagues to babysit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. A common practice would be to have somebody in the nursery, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Do you dispute that it was you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I have no memory of that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, I know, but do you dispute the evidence that it was you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I -- I don't know how I can answer that, sorry.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I don't... If I can't remember, I don't think I can say whether somebody else's recollection is right or not.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: How many babies of [Baby K]'s gestation had you seen before [Baby K] appeared in the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: In the Countess of Chester?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Very few, if any.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Was she a memorable arrival?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember her?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No -- well, I remember the fact that we had a baby of that gestation on the unit, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you dispute that when Dr Jayaram walked into nursery 1, you were standing over [Baby K]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I have no recollection, so I can't confirm or deny.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you dispute that when Dr Jayaram walked into nursery 1, [Baby K] was desaturating?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Again, I can't comment. I have no memory.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you dispute that the saturation monitor was down into the 80s?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I have no memory.
blocks.speaker: LETBY
